signature: :   “IOHANN ((*)) IOSEPH ((*)) SCHMIED ((*)) MACHTS ((*)) IN  ((*)) PFAFFEN DORFF ((*)) 1789 ((*)) ((O)) ((*)) ((O)) ((*))”; festoon pattern
pitch: B-flat, very sharp, with slide fully closed; with slide extended 44mm, solid B-flat (perhaps very slightly flat).
mouthpiece: Probably 20th century; funnel shape, rounded rim.
dimensions: bo1 11, bo2 11,  mp rcvr 12.3, slide sec. exit 10.3, slide sec. 1604, bell sec. 1055.5, o’lap 35, total le 2624.5, bell sec. entry 12.7, be 131, garland 29 (axial), garland 36 (along surface of bell). Measured by the author 2/12/99.
provenance: Moravian tradition suggests that the four Schmied (Schmidt) trombones in Gnadenhutten--17891, 17892, 17893, and 1804—were acquired from Lititz when that community purchased a new set.
remarks: Very nice sound, free-blowing; slide very stiff. Immoveable slide stay not telescopic; ferrules as in 17891; saddle with sheet-metal-style ring on slide bow; saddle has zigzag pattern on periphery and in center; flat bow guard covers termination of saddle; bumper on bow guard is raised in two stages; matching pair of X’s (to show alignment of slide) as in 17891; seam in bell clearly visible at 3 o’clock from player’s perspective; bell seam is even visible through garland; saddle with ring in bellbow matches that in slide bow; guard in bell bow doesn’t perfectly match guard in slide bow; guard in bell bow covers termination of saddle; flat bell stay (no eyelet) matches 17891; collar on bellpipe side of bell stay (later repair); fairly sharp terminal flare in bell. 17891 17892 and 17893 constitute a set; the soprano trombone 1804, by Johann Joseph Schmied’s son Johann Simon Schmidt, was undoubtedly used with the three 1789 instruments.
